note: Inclusive/exclusive comparisons in src/engine that no test holds.
A boundary is 'held' when flipping <= to < (or >= to >) makes a test fail. On
2026-08-30 forty-seven of sixty-eight were not held. This list should SHRINK,
and on 2026-08-31 it did, three times: nine, then seven, then ten, leaving
twenty-one. Only a NEW entry fails the check -- the backlog is a backlog, not a
monthly alarm, and an alarm that always fires is not an alarm.

ALL TWENTY-ONE SURVIVORS ARE CLASSIFIED, and none of them is a coverage gap.
`npm run check:boundaries:classify` flips each one again and re-runs the engine
over the values its comparisons test (scripts/observe-engine.ts) instead of the
suite. Every one of the twenty-one moved NOTHING the probe observes -- the
branch and its `else` compute the same answer at that point, so no test can
hold them and asking for one is asking for a fixture that manufactures a
difference. Every survivor's verdict is 'no observed difference'; zero are
observable, and there is no known case left unwritten.
That verdict is evidence, not proof: absence of a difference over a finite probe
is not a guarantee that none exists. What makes it worth trusting is the
calibration. All forty-seven HELD boundaries are visible to the same probe --
they must be, since a test distinguishes them -- and the report fails loudly
when one is not. It did fail, twice, on the first runs: eight held comparisons
were invisible because the probe stood near their thresholds rather than on
them, and one because a fixture used a shape `DeadlineDue` does not have and a
cast let it compile. Both were the probe's fault, both were found by the
calibration rather than by a person, and the check now refuses to be believed
until they are fixed.
What each one is, since the shape is worth recognising:
THE ENDPOINT THAT AGREES WITH THE RAMP. A linear phase-out short-circuits at
its endpoints, and the interpolation computes exactly the same value at those
very points. educationCredits 56/57, brackets 202 (Oregon's federal-tax-
deduction phase-out) and 231 (the Arkansas and Connecticut recapture ramps),
and fafsa 71/76. Six of the twenty-one, one shape.
THE GUARD THE LOOP REPEATS. These are defensive guards, not lines anybody
experiences. brackets 20 (`taxable <= 0`, where the loop's own first
comparison breaks at zero anyway), costBasis 46 (the next lot takes zero
shares and the `take > 0` guard drops it), iraDeduction 86 (unreachable: a
MAGI at or above the range's high end returns first), and finance 135 and
1263 -- the famous one. `debtPayoff`'s 'a payment that cannot cover the
interest never retires the debt' looks like the most consequential line in
the file and is not a decision at all: both loops end with `if (bal > 0)
return null`, so the early return is a FAST PATH worth 1,200 iterations of
no-op decimal math.
THE SPLIT POINT. amt 67, where at the 28% breakpoint the two-rate formula
reduces to the one-rate formula, and finance 736, a loan paid off in exactly
its term. Also finance 653, a spend at exactly the deductible.
THE ARM THAT IS ALREADY TRUE. benefits 352: the shipped ACA table covers from
0% FPL, so `!acaCovered(pct)` only fires above 400% FPL, where the `pct >= 100`
guard beside it is trivially true. benefits 166: past the allotment table's top
the fallback adds the per-person amount times (size - top), which is zero AT
top. finance 330 looks like its sibling at 311 and is not -- 311 DIVIDES by n
and overflows without its guard, while 330 multiplies by (1 - (1+r)^-0) = 0.
THE ONE UNHOLDABLE THROUGH THE PUBLIC API. dueDates 21's UPPER half guards a
fourth or fifth January Monday from being called Martin Luther King Jr. Day,
and no 1040-ES date falls on January 21. Its lower half is held, and matters:
when January 15 IS a Monday the Q4 payment moves to the 16th. Holding the
upper half would mean exporting `isMlkDay` to test an internal, which is a
worse trade than leaving one line on this list.
They stay listed rather than deleted. A branch can stop being redundant -- amt
67 would, the day its second term gained a constant -- and the classifier is
what would notice.
